comparisons.peer_summary: Other income (expense), net totaled $181 million in 2024, down from $197 million in 2023, primarily due to decreased interest income from lower short-term investment balances; this line item is primarily comprised of interest income from short-term investments, changes in valuation of equity investments, and foreign currency transaction gains and losses.

comparisons.peer_topic: Components of Interest and Other, Net
comparisons.peer_summary: In 2024, interest and other, net decreased due to higher interest expense from increased average borrowings and a decrease in other, net. The change in other, net included a $755 million loss from a derivative related to potential liquidated damages with Apollo and a $560 million benefit from interest related to an EC competition matter.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies discuss the components and drivers of 'Other, net'. NVDA attributes changes to non-affiliated investment values and foreign currency. INTC discusses 'other, net' as part of 'interest and other, net', highlighting specific significant items like derivative losses ($755 million) and interest benefits ($560 million). While NVDA focuses on investment valuation changes, INTC discloses more granular, idiosyncratic items (derivatives, regulatory interest) that drive the 'other' component, showing a difference in the nature of the non-operating income/expense drivers.

sentences.text: Change in Other, net, compared to fiscal year 2023 was driven by changes in value from our non-affiliated investments.
In 2024, interest and other, net decreased primarily due to higher interest expense due to higher 2024 average borrowings and lower other, net.

Included in other, net in 2024 is a loss of $755 million from the change in fair value of a non-designated derivative related to our assessed probability of paying construction-related liquidated damages to Apollo, our Ireland SCIP partner.

In 2024, we also received and recognized $560 million as a benefit to other, net for interest in relation to the European Commission competition matter for which we recorded and paid a ruling amount to the European Commission in 2009 and that we were successful at challenging and overturning with the ruling amount refunded to us in 2022.
